research_question: Can a UCIe fault confined to one virtual ECU increase shared-resource occupancy enough to cause a safety-critical transaction from another, error-free virtual ECU to miss its deadline?

interpretation: A fault confined to Guest A caused an otherwise deadline-compliant Guest B transaction to violate its real-time requirement through contention for a shared UCIe transmission resource. Guest B experienced no CRC errors and no replay, committed exactly once, and completed successfully, but exceeded its experimental timing budget because Guest A’s replay traffic retained the shared transmit resource. Functional isolation did not imply temporal isolation in this shared UCIe-based virtualized configuration.

bars.label: Guest B shared / Guest A faulty
